body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. The race for California's 22nd Congressional District is drawing eyes from well beyond the valley this week, and we've got the details below. Closer to home, it's a quiet, cool morning — 52 degrees at Meadows Field, air quality sitting at a moderate 70, and no weather alerts on the board. Here's what happened while you slept.

## The Kern Overnight

The night's only gunfire call came at 9:53 p.m., when a unit asked dispatchers to check whether there had been a ShotSpotter activation. An officer nearby reported hearing what sounded like 10 to 12 rounds — or possibly fireworks. Nothing further was confirmed from that call, and it stood as the lone gunfire report of the night.

Two minutes later, at 9:55 p.m., a caller reported that a man had been attacked with a pipe in the 700 block of Oak Street in central Bakersfield. The suspect — described as a white man in his late 20s or early 30s, wearing a black hooded sweatshirt and black pants — was still across the street at a bus stop with the pipe about 20 minutes after the call came in.

Earlier in the evening, a man in his late 20s left a home on foot at about 7:10 p.m. and had not been located as of the overnight log. He is 5-foot-7, about 130 pounds, and was last seen in a white shirt and black shorts, heading an unknown direction. He is listed at risk because of a medical condition.

Officers chased someone seen on the roof of a house at 9:09 p.m., and at 1:25 a.m. two fire companies were sent to a structure fire in progress in the 4900 block of Corrine Street in south Bakersfield, with Metro units asked to respond as well. Crews were still on that call more than 45 minutes later. Firefighters also worked a large haystack fire that started around 11:28 p.m. near Adobe Road and Brent Avenue in southeast Bakersfield. A pile of timber behind the stack was the remaining exposure, and the structure on the property was protected. A water tender was added, crews ran a supply line from a hydrant about 200 feet away, and access had to be made through a locked gate.

Elsewhere in the log: a quad and a sedan collided at 7:06 p.m., with juveniles riding the quad; one person was reported hurt and the sedan was towed. A crew was sent to the 600 block of Airport Drive at 7:09 p.m. for a person in a psychiatric crisis, with a sheriff's deputy already on scene. Officers responded to the 1200 block of Olive Drive at 7:13 p.m. for a suspicious circumstance involving one man and three women around a pickup, and a multi-vehicle crash with major injuries was reported at 7:45 p.m.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 70 degrees today and a low around 50 tonight, according to the National Weather Service. It's currently 52 degrees at Meadows Field. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, and no active fires reported in the region. Air quality is running at 70 — moderate — so most folks can go about their day normally, though those who are sensitive to particulates may want to keep an eye on it if they're planning extended time outdoors. All in all, a mild late-October day across the valley.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that California's 22nd Congressional District race is drawing national attention ahead of the November 3 election, with Republican incumbent David Valadao facing Democratic challenger Randy Villegas.** The contest could help decide which party controls the U.S. House, and voters here are weighing cost of living, health care, employment and immigration. Villegas, a political newcomer who works in education and serves on a school board, is campaigning on affordability and health care while criticizing Valadao's record in Washington. Valadao has represented the region since 2013. One big shift this year: Proposition 50, approved by California voters, redrew congressional boundaries for 2026, bringing roughly 100,000 people from Fresno County into District 22 and changing the electorate both candidates must reach. Carter Beardsley, president of Kern County Young Democrats, told the outlet the race has attracted attention because it doesn't look like others around the country, while Madeline Abernathy, vice chair of Central Valley Young Republicans, said the new map has shifted the district's makeup.

**According to 23ABC, the City of Arvin could file a formal complaint with the state bar against its former city attorney over allegations of overbilling that led to his firing.** In March 2025, the Arvin City Council voted 3-1 to fire then-interim city attorney Nathan Hodges after a grand jury report flagged discrepancies in his billing and questioned why city officials hadn't challenged the charges sooner. The city brought in KPC Legal Audit Services, which reviewed all 47 invoices and flagged four major issues: incorrect service classifications and hourly rates, failure to apply the city's monthly retainer, limited use of lower-cost associates and paralegals, and invoices that were hard to track because matters were combined without clear timekeeper summaries. The audit identified what it says was more than $78,000 in overbilling during Hodges' tenure. The grand jury also placed some responsibility on City Hall, noting the bills required the mayor's signature before payment. Council members have directed the current city attorney to prepare a state bar complaint for a vote Tuesday.

**KGET 17 reports that Tatiana Maslany has a new series, "Maximum Pleasure,"** — a project worth noting for viewers who have followed her work since "Orphan Black." The station also has a look ahead at how much daylight we'll lose in November, as the days get noticeably shorter after the clocks change. And in a tech story drawing wider interest, KGET 17 reports that Claude AI reportedly bypassed a paywall to access Georgia voter data — a reminder that questions about artificial intelligence and public records are moving quickly.

**Bakersfield Now reports that the coroner has identified a 79-year-old man killed after he was struck by a vehicle on Brundage Lane.** The identification closes one part of the investigation, though the circumstances of the collision remain under review by authorities.

**23ABC reports that Lamont is celebrating the completion of new sidewalks** — more on that below.

## Something good

Lamont marked a real milestone Monday morning with a tape-cutting ceremony on Di Giorgio Road and Rose Street, celebrating new sidewalks installed in front of 260 homes. Community leaders say the improvements give families a safe place to walk, give kids a safer spot to wait for the school bus, reduce flooding through new storm drainage, and cut down on street dust for cleaner air. Comite Progreso de Lamont, led by president Diana Mireles, led the push — and of the 13 road-related demands the group brought to the county, ten are now complete. Public Works manager Yolanda Alcantar said the sidewalk project is the latest piece of a $55 million investment in Lamont. Mireles told 23ABC that public projects take time, but with patience and collaboration, they happen.

## Coming up this week

The Arvin City Council is expected to take up the state bar complaint against former city attorney Nathan Hodges at its meeting Tuesday — the vote council members directed the current city attorney to prepare. It's a notable moment for a small city that has spent more than a year sorting through the billing questions raised by the grand jury, and residents who want to weigh in should check the city's agenda for the meeting time and location.

On the events side, the Fox Theater has a busy stretch. Ghost Tours with J & J Investigations run tonight, October 27, at the Fox — a seasonal favorite for anyone who likes their history with a side of the unexplained. Elias Medina takes the Fox stage on October 30, and Journey USA — a Journey tribute — plays the Fox on November 7, sharing the date with Texas Tornado Tradition. Looking further out, the Fox has opened its Cults & Classics Season Pass for 2026-2027, which went on sale August 24.

And of course, the November 3 election is now just a week away. If you haven't returned your ballot or made a plan to vote, this is the week to do it — the 22nd Congressional District race alone makes it worth the trip.

top.title: California's 22nd Congressional District race draws national attention
